explain.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a gear train. Count the teeth on the driver gear and the small gear; that ratio is the whole secret of gear speed and torque. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Gears: spur, helical, bevel and worm, and how the gear ratio works

explain.say: The teeth mesh one by one, so both gears move the same number of teeth each second. The big gear has three times the teeth, so it turns three times slower. Gear ratio is driven teeth over driver teeth: 60 over 20, which is 3. Output speed: 1500 over 3, that is 500 rpm. Which way does the big gear turn?

explain.say: The opposite way! And here is the payoff. Power is torque times speed, and almost none is lost, so a third of the speed means three times the torque. The motor gives 10 newton metres; out comes about 29, since a spur pair is about 98 percent efficient. Gears trade speed for torque.

explain.say: Gear types fit different jobs. See the groups? Spur gears have straight teeth: simple but noisy. Helical gears have slanted teeth that engage gradually, so they are quiet, but push sideways along the shaft. Bevel gears turn the drive through an angle; a worm gives huge ratios in one step. What turns rotation into a straight line?

draw.text: Helical teeth: smoother and quieter, but create axial thrust

explain.say: A rack and pinion, as in a car steering rack! Excellent work. Exam tip: for a gear train multiply the ratios of each pair; an idler gear between two others changes the direction but not the ratio. Challenge: what ratio do a 15-tooth pinion and a 45-tooth gear give?

draw.text: Train ratio = product of each pair ratio

faq.q: How do I calculate gear ratio?
faq.a: Divide the number of teeth on the driven gear by the teeth on the driving gear. Output speed is input speed divided by the ratio, and output torque is roughly input torque times the ratio.

faq.q: Why does a gearbox increase torque?
faq.a: Power is torque times speed and gears lose very little of it, so slowing the output by a ratio multiplies the torque by nearly the same ratio.

faq.q: What is the difference between spur and helical gears?
faq.a: Spur gears have teeth parallel to the shaft and are simple but noisy. Helical gears have angled teeth that mesh gradually, running quieter and carrying more load, but they push the shaft sideways.

faq.q: What is a worm gear used for?
faq.a: A worm and wheel gives a large reduction in one step, often 20 to 1 or more, between crossing shafts. Many worm drives cannot be driven backwards, which is useful in lifts and hoists.

faq.q: What does an idler gear do?
faq.a: An idler sits between two gears. It reverses the direction of the output but does not change the overall ratio.

facts: Two meshing external gears always turn in opposite directions.
A good pair of spur gears transmits about 98 % of the power.
